ETag.description: The resource's version, quoted (for example `"3"`). Send it back as If-Match on the next change.

Link.description: RFC 8288 link to the next page (`rel="next"`); absent on the last page.

X-Correlation-Id.description: The request's correlation id: echoed from the request header when valid, otherwise generated.

X-Next-Cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page; absent on the last page. Pass it as the `cursor` query parameter.

BadRequest.description: Bad Request: the request is malformed or a field is invalid; `errors` maps each field to its messages.

Forbidden.description: Forbidden: the caller lacks the permission (code `auth.forbidden`).

NotFound.description: Not Found: no such resource, or it is outside the caller's scope, or its module is disabled (code `module.disabled`).

PreconditionFailed.description: Precondition Failed: the If-Match version is stale; read the resource again.

PreconditionRequired.description: Precondition Required: the If-Match header is missing.

ServiceUnavailable.description: Service Unavailable: a dependency is briefly unavailable; retry after Retry-After seconds.

TooManyRequests.description: Too Many Requests: wait for Retry-After seconds.

AuditLogDto.description: One audit row as the read API returns it. Values were masked when the row was written (ADR-010), so nothing here can be un-masked. Changes is `{ "field": { "old": ..., "new": ... } }`; Metadata holds extras such as the command name.

CreateCustomerRequest.description: Body of a customer create. `UserId` (the owner) is honoured only for callers with effective CUSTOMERS_ALL.

CreateWebhookSubscriptionRequest.description: Body of POST /webhooks/subscriptions. The secret is generated by the server.

CustomerDto.description: The customer as returned to clients. `Version` is also sent as the `ETag`.

DevWebhookReceiptDto.description: The sink's answer to a delivery: `accepted` the first time, `duplicate` when the event id was already seen (at-least-once delivery).

GroupDto.description: A group with the roles its members inherit and how many members it has.

MeDto.description: The caller's own identity and what they may do, for the console's navigation and permission checks. Everything here is about the authenticated user only; nothing identifies anyone else.

displayName.description: Name to show in the UI.

groups.description: Codes of the active groups the user belongs to. Sorted.

modules.description: The modules that are effectively enabled right now (switched on in configuration and in the database).

permissions.description: Effective permission codes, the same set the API enforces: role grants plus unexpired allow overrides, minus unexpired deny overrides, with permissions of disabled modules removed. Sorted.

roles.description: Codes of the active roles the user holds, directly or through an active group. Sorted.

tenantId.description: The tenant, or null when tenancy is off or the user has none.

MeModuleDto.description: An enabled module as the console's navigation needs it.

ModuleDto.description: A module as the admin API shows it: the configuration switch, the runtime (database) switch, and the result. `Effective` is true only when both are on. `Version` is the ETag.

OverrideDto.description: A per-user allow or deny of one permission. `Expired` is evaluated against the clock at read time. `Version` is the ETag a later PUT or DELETE sends back in `If-Match`.

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code, such as customer.not_found. Clients branch on this, never on the title.

correlationId.description: The request's X-Correlation-Id (echoed, or generated when the client sent none).

tenantId.description: The caller's tenant, present only when tenancy is on and the caller is authenticated.

traceId.description: W3C trace id of the request, for finding it in the logs.

ReceivedWebhookDto.description: One webhook the Development sink accepted: verified signature, fresh timestamp, first time this event id was seen.

SetSinkSecretRequest.description: Body of PUT /dev/webhook-sink/secret: the signing secret the Development sink should trust.

TokenDto.description: The token response. `RefreshToken` is shown once and never stored in clear.

UpdateCustomerRequest.description: Body of a customer replace; the route carries the id and `If-Match` the version.

UpdateWebhookSubscriptionRequest.description: Body of PUT /webhooks/subscriptions/{id}. Requires If-Match. The secret is changed only by rotating it.

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code, such as customer.not_found. Clients branch on this, never on the title.

correlationId.description: The request's X-Correlation-Id (echoed, or generated when the client sent none).

tenantId.description: The caller's tenant, present only when tenancy is on and the caller is authenticated.

traceId.description: W3C trace id of the request, for finding it in the logs.

WebhookDeliveryDto.description: One delivery attempt state. No headers, no body, no secret: the clipped error is the only free text.

WebhookSubscriptionDto.description: A subscription as returned to clients. It never carries the secret; `Version` is also sent as the `ETag`.

WebhookSubscriptionSecretDto.description: The ONLY place the secret leaves the system: the response to create and to rotate. It is not stored in the clear and cannot be read again, so the caller must keep it. Use `WebhookSecretFormat` to sign and verify.

Bearer.description: Access token from `POST /api/v1/auth/token`. Permissions are looked up per request, so a role change takes effect immediately.

info.description: REST API of Fugue. Every error is an RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` body with a stable `code`. Mutations of a versioned resource need `If-Match` with the ETag of the last read. Lists are keyset paged: follow `X-Next-Cursor`. Send `X-Correlation-Id` (and optionally `X-Saga-Id`) to correlate calls; both are echoed. Authenticate with `POST /api/v1/auth/token` and send the access token as a Bearer token.
info.title: Fugue API

tags.description: The audit log (ADR-010): read-only, newest first, keyset paged. There is no write, update or delete endpoint, and the table refuses them anyway (append-only trigger). One-liners only.
tags.name: Audit

tags.description: Token issuance. Anonymous by necessity; both rate limits run before any password work.
tags.name: Auth

tags.description: Customers: a stateful aggregate rehearsing ETag/If-Match, keyset paging and guarded transitions. One-liners only.
tags.name: Customers

tags.description: A receiver for the signed webhooks, for ONE-process demos (ADR-011, D-040). Development only: any other environment answers 404. `POST` is anonymous on purpose (the sender has no JWT; the signature is the credential) and implements the receiver algorithm from the runbook: verify, reject stale timestamps, dedupe on the event id. Tell it the secret with `PUT .../secret`, read what arrived with `GET`.
tags.name: DevWebhookSink

tags.description: The one real endpoint of the scaffold: proves the pipeline end to end and gives the runbooks something to call.
tags.name: Diagnostics

tags.description: Groups: members inherit the group's roles. Minimal administration; every change writes a grant_audit row.
tags.name: Groups

tags.description: The signed-in caller's own identity and effective access. Needs no permission: every authenticated user may read their own.
tags.name: Me

tags.description: Module management (ADR-009): see the configuration, database and effective state, and flip the runtime switch.
tags.name: Modules

tags.description: Per-user permission overrides: an explicit allow or deny, optionally expiring. Deny wins over allow wins over role.
tags.name: Overrides

tags.description: Outbound webhook subscriptions (ADR-011): CRUD plus secret rotation. The secret appears only in the create and rotate responses, never again. One-liners only; every action needs `WEBHOOKS_MANAGE` (admin by default).
tags.name: Webhooks
